data.text/markdown:
overnight_open · one night, up close

What a stock did between yesterday's close and today's first trading hour, minute by minute, and what was known before the open. Pick a stock and one of its nights. The companion notebook overnight_open_study_marimo.py asks whether any of it adds up over ~530 stocks. The night (New York time):
part when what we have
previous days up to yesterday's close daily bars: moves, ranges, volume, ATR
after-hours 16:01-19:59 1-minute bars
overnight 20:00-04:00 no trades: only the price jump across it, and its volume (*)
pre-market 04:00-09:29 1-minute bars
news previous session + night SEC 8-Ks (timed to the second), headlines (dated)
(*) Overnight trades are reported late, at 08:00-08:09: their volume counts as overnight trading, their prices are stale and ignored. Benzinga headlines carry a date but no time. The first trading hour (09:30-10:29) is the outcome, measured from the official opening print (what a market-on-open order gets).
  1. The night table: built once for all ~530 stocks and cached. The first time takes about half an hour: the 1-minute bars month by month, then the SEC filings name by name.
  2. One night: its minute candles, the filings and the headlines.
  3. Its signals: each one against the stock's own normal, and which flags fired.
  4. All of the stock's nights: did the first hour follow the night?

1 · The night table

One row per stock and session: every signal known before 09:30 and what the first hour did. The columns are listed in research.FEATURES; moves are in units of the stock's daily ATR (its typical daily range), volumes against the stock's own mean of the 20 sessions before.
126,050 nights of 535 stocks, 2025-07-08 → 2026-06-26.

2 · One night

Flags mark an unusual night. A move flag fires when the after-hours or the pre-market moved at least move daily ATRs away from the close (either way). A volume flag fires when the after-hours, the 08:00 late reports or the pre-market traded at least volume times the stock's own normal. The news flags fire on an SEC 8-K accepted during the night (16:00 to 09:30), on one carrying earnings (Item 2.02), or on at least headlines times the usual number of Benzinga headlines dated the day before (and at least 3 of them).
